subject: A better X and Y error bar solution?

messages.author: f6aff3ab0165e685
messages.subject: A better X and Y error bar solution?
parts:
Hi, 
I was wondering why error bars are they way they are in ggplot. Why do we have to tell geom_errorbar what and where to draw? Why doe sit not behave more like geom_boxplot, which takes in a frame of observations and calculates the necessary statistics for plotting. Why is it two functions (_errorbar and errorbarh) instead of one that has an argument indicating direction(s)? Just curious if anyone can provide some background on the history / reasoning behind it.

Thanks,
Thomas

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: A better X and Y error bar solution?
parts:
A partial answer is that stat_summary() does most of what you're
asking for; its default geom is geom_pointrange (which Tufte-snobs like
me tend to prefer to geom_errorbar), and it offers a variety of choices
for how to compute the ranges (i.e., handy things to specify as the
fun.data argument: see ?mean_cl_boot). This isn't very well documented
in the body of the help text, but the examples are useful.

As for the two (vertical and horizontal) versions: I think this is
mostly historical. The very nice ggstance package now provides
horizontal versions of a lot of geoms.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: A better X and Y error bar solution?
parts:
There's not just one possible calculation for error bars, but an
infinity of possibilities depending on the model. Boxplots, on
the other hand, have one defined calculation.

Hadley
